sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上奇妙有趣的事物，同时提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the history of fire.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊聊火的历史。

sentences.en: We humans are the only animal on Earth that has truly mastered fire: that has learned to keep it, make it, cook with it, and build entire civilisations around it.
sentences.zh: 我们人类是地球上唯一真正掌握了火的动物：学会了保存火、制造火、用火烹饪，并围绕火建立起整个人类文明。

sentences.en: And today, we are going to trace that story.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们就来追溯这段历史。

sentences.en: How fire changed our bodies, our minds, the way we interact with one another, and made the modern world possible.
sentences.zh: 火如何改变了我们的身体、思维以及彼此互动的方式，并让现代世界成为可能。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们一分钟也不浪费，直接切入正题。

sentences.en: There is a cave in South Africa called Wonderwerk.
sentences.zh: 南非有一个叫 Wonderwerk 的洞穴。

sentences.en: The name means "miracle" in Afrikaans. This cave contains up to 7 metres of sediment, deposits, layers that had built up, millimetre by millimetre, over hundreds of thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 这个名字在南非语中是“奇迹”的意思。这个洞穴包含长达 7 米的沉积物，这些堆积物和地层历经几十万年，一毫米一毫米地累积起来。

sentences.en: Like a huge tower of human, and even pre-human, history.
sentences.zh: 就像一座巨大的人类、甚至前人类历史的宝塔。

sentences.en: About one metre down, in a layer dating to roughly one million years ago, researchers from Boston University found charred plant material and burned bone fragments.
sentences.zh: 在大约一米深、可以追溯到大约一百万年前的地层中，波士顿大学的研究人员发现了烧焦的植物材料和燃烧过的骨头碎片。

sentences.en: Both had been heated to temperatures of around 500 degrees Celsius, almost 1,000 degrees Fahrenheit.
sentences.zh: 两者都被加热到约 500 摄氏度的高温，也就是将近 1,000 华氏度。

sentences.en: This was not a wildfire that swept through.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一场掠过森林的野火。

sentences.en: The burning had happened inside the cave, repeatedly, over time, in the same spot.
sentences.zh: 燃烧是发生在洞穴内部的，随着时间的推移，在同一个地点反复发生。

sentences.en: It was the oldest known fireplace in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是世界上已知最古老的炉灶。

sentences.en: The creatures who most probably made this fire were called Homo erectus.
sentences.zh: 最有可能生起这团火的生物被称为直立人。

sentences.en: That name, as the Latin scholars among you will know, simply means upright human.
sentences.zh: 正如你们当中的拉丁语学者所知，这个名字的意思很简单，就是直立的人。

sentences.en: They were not Homo sapiens, not quite us.
sentences.zh: 他们不是智人，还算不上是我们。

sentences.en: Their brains were smaller, their bones heavier, their foreheads thick and heavy.
sentences.zh: 他们的脑容量较小，骨骼更沉重，前额厚重。

sentences.en: But they walked on two legs, they made stone tools, and, importantly for what we're talking about today, they used fire.
sentences.zh: 但他们用两足行走，制作石器，而且对我们今天讨论的话题至关重要——他们会用火。

sentences.en: Now, nobody knows exactly when the first of our ancestors started using fire; one million years ago is simply as far back as the reliable evidence goes.
sentences.zh: 现在，没有人确切知道我们的祖先是什么时候开始用火的；一百万年前只是可靠证据能够追溯到的最远时间。

sentences.en: What we do know is that for a very long period, our ancestors were not making fire.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，在很长的一段时间里，我们的祖先并不是自己生火。

sentences.en: They were finding it. Fire breaks out in the wild, as it always has and always will.
sentences.zh: 他们是去寻找火。火在野外爆发，过去如此，将来也一直如此。

sentences.en: Lightning strikes a dry tree. A lava flow ignites grassland.
sentences.zh: 闪电击中干燥的树木。熔岩流点燃了草原。

sentences.en: Dry grass catches in the heat of a long summer.
sentences.zh: 漫长夏日的炎热使干燥的草木起火。

sentences.en: And almost every animal on Earth, when this happens, does the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而当这种事情发生时，地球上几乎所有的动物都会做同一件事。

sentences.en: It runs. Fire is scary. It's hot. Instinct kicks in, and even the fiercest predator will run in the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 逃跑。火是可怕的。它是热的。本能驱使着它们，甚至最凶猛的掠食者也会朝着相反的方向狂奔。

sentences.en: Homo erectus did something different. At some point, they approached.
sentences.zh: 直立人却做了不同的事。在某个时刻，他们靠近了。

sentences.en: Perhaps they picked up a burning branch and carried it back.
sentences.zh: 也许他们捡起了一根燃烧的树枝把它带了回去。

sentences.en: Perhaps they found smouldering wood and kept it alive.
sentences.zh: 也许他们发现了阴燃的木头并让它不灭。

sentences.en: However it happened, the crucial step was this: they stopped merely fleeing fire and started managing it.
sentences.zh: 无论它是如何发生的，至关重要的一步是：他们不再仅仅逃避火，而是开始管理火。

sentences.en: Of course, this wasn't a simple task. As any seasoned camper will know, tending a fire and keeping it alight requires real effort.
sentences.zh: 当然，这不是一件简单的事。正如任何经验丰富的露营者所知，照看一炉火并让它持续燃烧需要付出真正的努力。

sentences.en: You have to find wood to burn, carry it, arrange it properly, and protect the flame from wind and rain.
sentences.zh: 你必须寻找要烧的木头，搬运它，妥善安排它，并保护火焰免受风吹雨打。

sentences.en: So keeping a fire alive required attention, planning, and cooperation.
sentences.zh: 因此，维持火种需要注意力、计划和合作。

sentences.en: It required something that looks, in other words, very much like care.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它需要一种看起来非常像关爱的东西。

sentences.en: And as for why Homo erectus would want to have a fire, well, there are numerous immediate benefits.
sentences.zh: 至于为什么直立人会想要生火，嗯，有许多立竿见影的好处。

sentences.en: Warmth through cold nights. Light to see by.
sentences.zh: 在寒冷的夜晚带来温暖。带来照明。

sentences.en: And perhaps most importantly, safety. A fire keeps large predators away.
sentences.zh: 或许最重要的是，安全。火能让大型捕食者退避三舍。

sentences.en: And in a world where leopards, lions, hyenas, and sabre-toothed cats were a constant menace, especially in the darkness of night, fire was a wonderful deterrent.
sentences.zh: 在一个豹子、狮子、鬣猫和剑齿虎构成持续威胁的世界里，特别是在黑夜中，火是一个极好的威慑力量。

sentences.en: But fire changed humans in ways that go far deeper than warmth and safety.
sentences.zh: 但火改变人类的方式，远比温暖和安全更为深远。

sentences.en: In 2009, a Harvard professor named Richard Wrangham published a book called Catching Fire: How Cooking Made Us Human.
sentences.zh: 2009年，哈佛大学教授理查德·兰厄姆出版了一本名为《生火：烹饪如何让我们成为人类》的书。

sentences.en: The argument, as you might guess from the title, is that cooking food rather than eating it raw is one of the fundamental differences between humans and every other animal.
sentences.zh: 正如你从书名中可能猜到的那样，他的论点是，烹饪食物而不是生吃食物，是人类与其他所有动物之间的根本区别之一。

sentences.en: And the consequences go far deeper than simply getting to enjoy a hotter, and dare I say, tastier meal.
sentences.zh: 其带来的影响远远超出了仅仅享受一顿更热、而且我敢说更美味的饭菜。

sentences.en: His argument is this. Raw food is hard to digest.
sentences.zh: 他的论点是这样的。生食很难消化。

sentences.en: Your body has to work extremely hard to extract calories from uncooked meats, roots, and plant material.
sentences.zh: 你的身体必须付出极大的努力才能从未煮熟的肉类、根茎和植物材料中提取热量。

sentences.en: Cooking changes all of that. It breaks down the cellular structure of food before it even enters your mouth.
sentences.zh: 烹饪改变这一切。它甚至在你将食物送入口中之前，就分解了食物的细胞结构。

sentences.en: Proteins unravel. Starches become easier to absorb.
sentences.zh: 蛋白质展开。淀粉更容易被吸收。

sentences.en: Tough fibres soften. And cooked food releases anywhere between 30 and 100 percent more calories than the same food eaten raw.
sentences.zh: 坚韧的纤维变软了。而且煮熟的食物释放的热量比生吃同样的食物多出 30% 到 100%。

sentences.en: So if you are getting more energy from the same amount of food, you do not need such a large, energy-hungry digestive system to process it.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你从等量的食物中获得更多的能量，你就不需要那么大、消耗大量能量的消化系统来处理它。

sentences.en: And the energy you are no longer spending on digestion becomes available for something else.
sentences.zh: 而你不再用于消化的能量，就可以腾出来用于其他事情。

sentences.en: Wrangham's argument is that this surplus energy went to the brain.
sentences.zh: 兰厄姆的论点是，这部分多余的能量滋养了大脑。

sentences.en: He points to Homo erectus, who appeared roughly 1.8 million years ago.
sentences.zh: 他指出了大约在 180 万年前出现的直立人。

sentences.en: Earlier hominins, like Australopithecus, had large guts, small brains, and big teeth suited to chewing tough, raw food.
sentences.zh: 更早的原始人，比如南方古猿，有着巨大的内脏、较小的大脑以及适合咀嚼坚硬生食的大牙齿。

sentences.en: Homo erectus had dramatically smaller teeth and a smaller gut.
sentences.zh: 直立人的牙齿和内脏明显要小得多。

sentences.en: But a noticeably larger brain. This shift happens at roughly the time we see the first signs of fire use.
sentences.zh: 但脑容量却显著增大。这种转变大约发生在人类最早出现用火迹象的时期。

sentences.en: Wrangham's claim is that this is not a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 兰厄姆断言，这绝非巧合。

sentences.en: Cooking made this transition possible. Perhaps cooking drove it.
sentences.zh: 烹饪使这种转变成为可能。也许烹饪正是推动力。

sentences.en: Now, not everyone agrees. Some researchers argue the energy came from raw meat and bone marrow.
sentences.zh: 当然，并非所有人都赞同这一点。一些研究人员认为，能量来自生肉和骨髓。

sentences.en: Their argument is that eating more animal protein, not cooking, explains the anatomical changes.
sentences.zh: 他们的论点是，吃更多的动物蛋白质，而不是烹饪，解释了这些解剖结构的变化。

sentences.en: But here is what is not in dispute: we are the only animal on earth that cooks its food.
sentences.zh: 但有一点是无可争议的：我们是地球上唯一烹饪食物的动物。

sentences.en: Chimpanzees are our closest living relatives.
sentences.zh: 黑猩猩是我们现存最近的亲戚。

sentences.en: They share roughly 98 percent of our DNA.
sentences.zh: 它们与我们共享大约 98% 的 DNA。

sentences.en: And they have never, in any documented setting, cooked anything.
sentences.zh: 而且在任何有记录的情况下，它们都从未烹饪过任何东西。

sentences.en: And it is not because they don't want to.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为它们不想这样做。

sentences.en: In a series of experiments by researchers at Harvard and Yale, chimpanzees were given a choice between a raw piece of food and a cooked one.
sentences.zh: 在哈佛和耶鲁研究人员的一系列实验中，黑猩猩在生食和熟食之间进行选择。

sentences.en: All 29 chimpanzees in the study chose the cooked option.
sentences.zh: 研究中的所有 29 只黑猩猩都选择了熟食。

sentences.en: And more strikingly: when the chimps were shown that they could place a raw piece of food into a device that would produce a cooked version afterwards, they were willing to wait.
sentences.zh: 更引人注目的是：当黑猩猩被告知，它们可以把一块生食物放进一个设备中，该设备随后会产出一份熟食时，它们愿意等待。

sentences.en: So even though they wanted to eat, they held back from eating the raw food, specifically in order to get the cooked version.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管它们很想吃，但它们克制住自己不吃生食，专门为了得到熟食。

sentences.en: So chimpanzees understand the transformation, from raw to cooked food.
sentences.zh: 所以黑猩猩理解从生食到熟食的转变。

sentences.en: They prefer the result. They will even delay gratification to get it.
sentences.zh: 它们喜欢这个结果。它们甚至愿意为了得到它而延迟满足。

sentences.en: They just don't know how to use or make fire.
sentences.zh: 它们只是不知道如何使用或制造火。

sentences.en: Humans do. And that single difference may be the most consequential in the entire history of life on Earth.
sentences.zh: 人类懂得。而这单一的区别，可能是地球生命史上最具影响力的事件。

sentences.en: Now, there is one more physical consequence of fire we need to talk about.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们还需要讨论火带来的另一个生理影响。

sentences.en: It concerns sleep. Before fire, our ancestors almost certainly slept in trees, as most great apes still do.
sentences.zh: 它关乎睡眠。在有火之前，我们的祖先几乎肯定睡在树上，就像大多数类人猿现在所做的那样。

sentences.en: Trees are safer from predators. But you don't have to have slept in many trees yourself to know that trees are not particularly comfortable places to spend the night.
sentences.zh: 树上对捕食者来说更安全。但你不用自己睡过很多树就知道，树绝对不是过夜的舒适地方。

sentences.en: You wake up frequently, you sleep lightly and uncomfortably.
sentences.zh: 你频繁醒来，睡眠很浅而且很不舒服。

sentences.en: Chimpanzees sleep around ten hours a night because their sleep is so frequently disturbed.
sentences.zh: 黑猩猩一晚睡大约十个小时，因为它们的睡眠经常被打断。

sentences.en: Humans sleep seven to eight hours. And we sleep deeply.
sentences.zh: 人类睡七到八个小时。而且我们睡得很深。

sentences.en: And to bring this back to fire, with a fire burning through the night, you could sleep on the ground and be safe.
sentences.zh: 把话题拉回到火上，有了整夜燃烧的火，你就可以睡在地上，并且是安全的。

sentences.en: And because you felt safe, and you were safe, you could sleep properly.
sentences.zh: 正因为你感到安全，而且你确实很安全，你才能睡好觉。

sentences.en: The deep, dreaming sleep that consolidates memory, repairs the body, and allows the brain to do its work.
sentences.zh: 这种巩固记忆、修复身体、让大脑发挥作用的深度做梦睡眠。

sentences.en: The depth of human sleep, tied to memory, learning, creativity, and health, may itself be, in part, a consequence of learning to manage fire.
sentences.zh: 人类睡眠的深度与记忆、学习、创造力以及健康息息相关，这本身或许部分就是学会掌控火的结果。

sentences.en: And by moving our beds from the branches to the ground, we created a new physical space: the circle.
sentences.zh: 通过把我们的床铺从树枝搬到地面，我们创造了一个新的物理空间：圆圈。

sentences.en: And it was in this circle, protected by the flames, that the second great transformation happened: we started to talk in a different way.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个由火焰保护的圆圈里，第二大转变发生了：我们开始用一种不同的方式交谈。

sentences.en: An anthropologist at the University of Utah named Polly Wiessner spent four decades studying a group of Kalahari Desert bushmen in southern Africa.
sentences.zh: 犹他大学的一位人类学家名叫波利·威斯纳，她花了四十年时间研究南部非洲卡拉哈里沙漠的一群布须曼人。

sentences.en: This group is one of the oldest-surviving hunter-gatherer cultures on earth.
sentences.zh: 这个群体是地球上现存最古老的狩猎采集文化之一。

sentences.en: She analysed hundreds of their conversations.
sentences.zh: 她分析了他们数百段对话。

sentences.en: And she found a very clear pattern. During the day, conversations were mostly practical.
sentences.zh: 她发现了一个非常清晰的模式。白天，对话大多是实用的。

sentences.en: Economic decisions. Disputes. Complaints.
sentences.zh: 经济决策。争端。抱怨。

sentences.en: Discussions about food and hunting. Around the fire at night, the topics were very different.
sentences.zh: 关于食物和狩猎的讨论。到了夜里围坐在火堆旁，话题就大不相同了。

sentences.en: Storytelling accounted for 81 percent of all conversations, compared to only 6 percent during the day.
sentences.zh: 讲故事占了所有对话的 81%，而白天仅占 6%。

sentences.en: At night, by firelight, people told stories about distant lands, about people they had never met, about ancestors and spirits and the distant past.
sentences.zh: 夜里，在火光下，人们讲述关于遥远土地的故事，关于他们从未见过的人的故事，关于祖先、精灵和遥远过去的故事。

sentences.en: They speculated about things they could not see.
sentences.zh: 他们推测着那些看不见的事物。

sentences.en: They laughed. They imagined. Many researchers argue this is where human language, storytelling, and imagination really grew, around the calm of the fire.
sentences.zh: 他们欢笑。他们幻想。许多研究人员认为，人类的语言、故事讲述和想象力，正是在火堆的平静氛围中真正成长起来的。

sentences.en: Stories bind communities. They carry knowledge across generations.
sentences.zh: 故事将社区凝聚在一起。它们跨越代际传递知识。

sentences.en: They let us think about distant places and people, past events, and futures that have not yet happened.
sentences.zh: 它们让我们思考遥远的地方和人物、过去的事件，以及尚未发生的未来。

sentences.en: And the fire restructured domestic life in practical ways too.
sentences.zh: 火也在实际层面上重构了家庭生活。

sentences.en: Cooking with fire requires different tasks: collecting the wood, starting the fire, tending the fire, doing the cooking, and, of course, someone still needs to go and hunt the unfortunate animal everyone is going to eat.
sentences.zh: 用火烹饪需要不同的任务：收集木材、生火、照看火、进行烹饪，当然，还需要有人去捕猎大家都要吃的倒霉动物。

sentences.en: This requires co-operation, specialisation, and division of labour.
sentences.zh: 这需要合作、专业化和劳动分工。

sentences.en: Often, though not always, cooking became associated more with women, and hunting more with men.
sentences.zh: 虽然并非总是如此，但通常烹饪更多地与女性联系在一起，而狩猎则更多地与男性联系在一起。

sentences.en: And Wrangham, in the book I mentioned earlier, makes another, more provocative suggestion.
sentences.zh: 兰厄姆在我前面提到的书中，提出了另一个更具挑衅性的建议。

sentences.en: He argues that cooking may have been one of the early drivers of pair bonding, of a more stable relationship between a man and a woman, based less on romantic love than on mutual advantage.
sentences.zh: 他认为，烹饪可能是男女之间建立伴侣关系、建立更稳定关系的早期推动力之一，这种关系更多地基于共同利益，而不是浪漫爱情。

sentences.en: Imagine a woman crouching over a fire, with cooked food in front of her.
sentences.zh: 想象一下一个女人蹲在火堆旁，面前摆着煮熟的食物。

sentences.en: That food was valuable. It had taken time to prepare.
sentences.zh: 那食物很有价值。它需要时间来准备。

sentences.en: And because it was soft, warm, and ready to eat, it could also be stolen.
sentences.zh: 而且因为它又软、又热、随时可以食用，它也很容易被偷走。

sentences.en: Wrangham’s argument is that a man could provide protection, especially from other members of the group, in exchange for a share of that cooked food.
sentences.zh: 兰厄姆的论点是，男人可以提供保护，特别是免受群体中其他成员的伤害，以此来换取一部分煮熟的食物。

sentences.en: Over time, he suggests, this practical arrangement may have helped shape something closer to human pair bonding: not marriage as we understand it today, but an early form of domestic partnership.
sentences.zh: 他认为，随着时间的推移，这种实际的安排可能有助于塑造更接近人类伴侣关系的东西：不是我们今天所理解的婚姻，而是早期形式的家庭伙伴关系。

sentences.en: It is, I should stress, simply a theory, but an interesting one nonetheless, that the first human couples got together and stayed together in order to protect their dinner.
sentences.zh: 我必须强调，这只是一种理论，但尽管如此，它很有趣，即第一批人类伴侣走到一起并保持在一起是为了保护他们的晚餐。

sentences.en: So, for hundreds of thousands of years, then, early humans found fire, kept it, and built their lives around it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在几十万年的时间里，早期人类发现火、保存火，并围绕火建立生活。

sentences.en: But, importantly, they were entirely at the mercy of finding it.
sentences.zh: 但重要的是，他们完全听天由命，取决于能否找到火。

sentences.en: If the flame went out, that was it. You had to wait for lightning to strike again, or travel far to find fire somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 如果火焰熄灭了，那就完了。你必须等待闪电再次击中，或者走很远的路去别处寻找火。

sentences.en: The warmth, the safety, the cooked food, the community — all of it depended on a flame that someone, somewhere, had to have been lucky enough to find.
sentences.zh: 温暖、安全、熟食、社区——这一切都取决于某人、某处碰巧幸运找到的火焰。

sentences.en: That dependence is what changed around 400,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这种依赖性在大约 40万 年前改变了。

sentences.en: We stopped waiting for the lightning, and learned how to make fire ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们不再等待闪电，而是学会了自己生火。

sentences.en: First, it's thought it was through percussion, striking pieces of flint against iron pyrite to create sparks that could catch in a small bundle of tinder: small, dry pieces of wood or leaves.
sentences.zh: 首先，人们认为是通过打击乐般的方法，用燧石敲击黄铁矿产生火花，这些火花可以点燃一小捆火绒：细小、干燥的木头或树叶。

sentences.en: Later came the friction method: spinning a dry wooden rod against a flat piece of softer wood until there's enough heat built up to set dry leaves or wood alight.
sentences.zh: 后来出现了摩擦法：将一根干燥的木棍对着一块较软的干木头旋转，直到积聚足够的热量来点燃干树叶或木头。

sentences.en: There is of course no way to know what it felt like when the first person, wherever he or she was, figured out how to create fire.
sentences.zh: 当然，当第一个人——无论他或她在哪里——弄清楚如何生火时，那种感觉是无法得知的。

sentences.en: But it must have felt like magic, like you had just figured out the secret to one of the world's greatest puzzles.
sentences.zh: 但那一定感觉像魔法一样，就像你刚刚解开了世界最大谜团之一的秘密。

sentences.en: And they had, really. But for most of the million-year story of fire, the fuel was simple.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们确实做到了。但在长达百万年的火的历史中，燃料很简单。

sentences.en: It was wood, for the most part. Sometimes dried grass, peat, charcoal, or animal dung.
sentences.zh: 大部分是木头。有时是干草、泥炭、木炭或动物粪便。

sentences.en: Things that had grown under the sun, stored its energy, and released it again as heat and light when they burned.
sentences.zh: 这些东西在阳光下生长，储存了它的能量，并在燃烧时以热量和光的形式再次释放出来。

sentences.en: And it was enough. Enough to build every civilisation before roughly 300 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这就足够了。足以支撑大约 300 年前之前的所有文明。

sentences.en: The ancient Egyptians, classical Greece, the Roman Empire, medieval Europe: all of it ran on burning wood and charcoal.
sentences.zh: 古埃及人、古典希腊、罗马帝国、中世纪欧洲：所有这一切都是靠燃烧木头和木炭运转的。

sentences.en: You could smelt metals, fire pottery, heat homes, cook food, and light streets.
sentences.zh: 你可以冶炼金属、烧制陶器、温暖房屋、烹饪食物和照亮街道。

sentences.en: Then, gradually, the wood started to run out.
sentences.zh: 然后，渐渐地，木头开始耗尽。

sentences.en: In Britain, by the 17th century, forests had been stripped.
sentences.zh: 在英国，到了 17 世纪，森林已经被砍伐殆尽。

sentences.en: Wood for building ships, for building houses, for heating: all of it was scarce and getting increasingly expensive.
sentences.zh: 用于建造船只、建造房屋、取暖的木材：所有这些都十分稀缺，而且变得越来越昂贵。

sentences.en: But people still needed fire, or rather, the heat that fire gave out.
sentences.zh: 但人们仍然需要火，或者更准确地说，需要火散发出的热量。

sentences.en: The answer was right under their noses, or to be precise, under their feet: coal, and later, oil.
sentences.zh: 答案就在他们眼皮底下，确切地说，就在他们脚下：煤炭，以及后来的石油。

sentences.en: Now, the existence of coal had been common knowledge for centuries.
sentences.zh: 其实，煤炭的存在几个世纪以来一直是常识。

sentences.en: It washed up on the beach, and you could collect it in small quantities from hillsides, or from relatively close to the surface.
sentences.zh: 它被冲上沙滩，你可以从山坡上以小批量收集它，或者从离地表相对较近的地方获取。

sentences.en: And people in northeast England and South Wales had been burning it in small quantities for generations.
sentences.zh: 英格兰东北部和南威尔士的人们世世代代一直在小批量地燃烧它。

sentences.en: But it was regarded as a poor substitute: dirtier, smellier, and compared to wood, which you just got from trees, it was much harder to get at in any sort of useful quantity.
sentences.zh: 但它被视为一种劣质替代品：更脏、更臭，而且与只需从树上获取的木材相比，以任何有用的数量获取它要困难得多。

sentences.en: But there wasn't an alternative; England was running out of trees, it was running out of wood.
sentences.zh: 但别无选择；英格兰的树木快要砍光了，木头快要用完了。

sentences.en: And this need, this desperation, was the first domino in the Industrial Revolution, and you could even argue every technological development that you and I benefit from today.
sentences.zh: 这种需求，这种绝望，是工业革命的第一张多米诺骨牌，你甚至可以说是你和我今天受益的每一项技术发展的起点。

sentences.en: In 1709, a man named Abraham Darby worked out how to make iron using coke, a purified, high-carbon form of coal.
sentences.zh: 1709 年，一个叫亚伯拉罕·达比的人研究出如何使用焦炭（一种经过提纯的高碳形式的煤）来炼铁。

sentences.en: This was the first time someone had managed to make iron with coal, rather than charcoal, burnt wood.
sentences.zh: 这是人类第一次设法用煤而不是用木炭、烧过的木头来炼铁。

sentences.en: And this had considerable advantages. Using coal was much cheaper.
sentences.zh: 这具有相当大的优势。使用煤炭要便宜得多。

sentences.en: It turned iron, and later steel, from scarce, expensive materials into industrial commodities.
sentences.zh: 它将铁、以及后来的钢，从稀缺、昂贵的材料变成了工业大宗商品。

sentences.en: And more importantly, coal appeared to be virtually limitless.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，煤炭似乎是几乎取之不尽的。

sentences.en: Before this, iron production was limited by the rate at which forests could grow back.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，铁的产量受到森林再生速度的限制。

sentences.en: After Darby, it was limited only by how fast you could dig.
sentences.zh: 而在达比之后，它仅受限于你挖得有多快。

sentences.en: And Britain dug very fast. In 1700, roughly five-sixths of all coal mined in the entire world came from Britain.
sentences.zh: 而英国人挖得非常快。1700 年，全球开采的所有煤炭中，大约有六分之五来自英国。

sentences.en: Annual iron output, which stood at around 2,500 tons in the early 1700s, reached 2.5 million tons by 1850.
sentences.zh: 年产铁量在 18 世纪初约为 2,500 吨，到 1850 年达到了 250 万吨。

sentences.en: A thousand-fold increase in just a century and a half.
sentences.zh: 在短短一个半世纪里增长了一千倍。

sentences.en: Now, I don't want to turn this into an episode about the Industrial Revolution [we already have one on that, it's episode number 150], but the main point is that this was primarily a fire revolution.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不想把这变成一集关于工业革命的节目（我们已经有一集关于这个了，那是第 150 集），但核心观点是，这主要是一场火的革命。

sentences.en: It was about inventing better and better ways to create energy, to create heat, and then transform that into different forms of energy and industrial output.
sentences.zh: 它是关于发明越来越好的方法来产生能量、产生热量，然后将其转化为不同形式的能量和工业产出。

sentences.en: And after that, came oil, which is an even more energy-dense fuel than coal, and being liquid, is far easier to transport.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，便是石油，它是一种能量密度比煤炭更高的燃料，而且由于是液体，运输起来要容易得多。

sentences.en: What followed was the fastest transformation of human life in the entire million-year story of fire.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是火的百万年历史中人类生活最快的转变。

sentences.en: Cars, aeroplanes, ships, factories, central heating, electric light: all of it, at its root, a consequence of setting fire to stuff and using its heat.
sentences.zh: 汽车、飞机、轮船、工厂、中央暖气、电灯：这一切，从根本上讲，都是点燃东西并利用其热量的结果。

sentences.en: Now, it would be remiss of me not to mention the environmental side-effects of all of this, the trillions of tonnes of CO2 this is all estimated to have released into the atmosphere, and what this might mean for the planet's future.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果我不提及所有这一切带来的环境副作用，那就太失职了，据估计，这一切向大气中释放了数万亿吨二氧化碳，以及这可能对地球未来意味着什么。

sentences.en: But to come back to where we started. Sometime around a million years ago, our early ancestors found fire in the wild and kept it burning.
sentences.zh: 但让我们回到我们开始的地方。大约在一百万年前，我们的早期祖先在野外发现了火并让它持续燃烧。

sentences.en: Then we learned how to make it ourselves.
sentences.zh: 然后我们学会了自己生火。

sentences.en: We used it to cook our food, shape our societies, and build things our ancestors could never have imagined.
sentences.zh: 我们用它来烹饪食物、塑造我们的社会，并建造了我们的祖先永远无法想象的东西。

sentences.en: Fire might seem like just another part of the natural world.
sentences.zh: 火可能看起来只是自然界的另一个部分。

sentences.en: But for us humans, it changed everything.
sentences.zh: 但对我们人类来说，它改变了一切。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on the history of fire.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天关于火的历史的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 我希望这是一期有趣的节目，并且你学到了新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: Let me know in the comments below, if you're listening somewhere where you can comment.
sentences.zh: 如果你在某个可以评论的地方收听，请在下方的评论区告诉我。

sentences.en: And for the members among you, you can head right into our community forum at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 对于会员朋友们，你们可以直接进入我们的社区论坛 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他充满好奇心的人畅所欲言。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，注意安全，我们下期节目见。
